title: Freeze canonical naming, layout, and layer-boundary standard
goal: Publish one authoritative standard for repository layout, file naming, controlled exceptions, and dependency directions.
statusNote: 2026-09-23: docs/designs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md (and its .en.md companion) extended into the single canonical standard with §5 file naming vocabulary, §6 document taxonomy, §7 generated-artifact rules, §8 layer dependency matrix, §9 controlled exceptions, and §10 gate mapping plus change procedure. Document-only change: no production code, no checker whitelist, no file moves. Verified with check-structure (0 findings/1939 files), task-packet template, frontmatter-check, harness doc-frontmatter strict (0 errors), doc-links (0 findings), and the structure-contract unit tests (11 pass). Unimplemented enforcement (generated marker, check:generated, platform->system / auth->iam blocking) is recorded as an explicit gap for the Wave 1 tasks.
technicalDebtNote: The standard names enforcement that does not exist yet: the generated-file marker and check:generated drift gate are unimplemented, check-arch-boundaries.mjs is not wired into CI, and platform -> system / auth -> system/iam dependencies are still unblocked. Each is assigned to a Wave 1 task rather than silently assumed to hold.
dependencyLayers: platform governance (repository layout, naming, boundary rules)

in: file suffix vocabulary (backend Go, frontend TS/TSX, docs)
generated artifact rules (source, output, hand layer, drift, marker)
controlled exceptions (auth/lowcode/generated) with owner and rationale
gate mapping and the standard-first change procedure
out: bulk file moves or document relocation
runtime behavior, API, database, permission, i18n changes

runtimeEvidence: not runtime-sensitive: documentation and governance only

humanGates: none required (documentation-only governance change) — PR gates + non-author review
